chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim. He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed a community went to a prophet of theirs and said: Ask your Lord to alleviate death from us. So he asked on their behalf, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, alleviated death from them. They multiplied until their homes became narrow for them, and the lineages proliferated. A man would wake up needing to feed his father, his mother, his grandfather, and his grandfather's grandfather, and to clean them and take care of them. They became too busy to seek a livelihood. So they came to him and said: Ask your Lord to return us to our lifespans as they were. So he asked his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and He returned them to their lifespans.

key_terms.آجال: Aajaal - appointed lifespans or terms of death, plural of ajal
key_terms.الموت: al-Mawt - death, the cessation of life ordained by God

ai.seo_question: What happened when a community asked their prophet to remove death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) relates the story of a people who asked their prophet to remove death from among them. God granted their wish, but soon they faced severe overcrowding, endlessly multiplying generations, and unbearable caretaking burdens. Unable to even seek a livelihood, they begged to have death restored. This parable illustrates divine wisdom in ordaining death: far from being a punishment, death is a mercy that maintains balance in human life. The original audience, in a culture that mourned death deeply, would have found comfort in understanding death's essential role in the divine order.
